$Comment: The occasional extras Trim Work turns up, beside the wage and the tools. Three rolls, all
bonuses: neither the deep find nor the boost token is anybody's reason for filling the order, and
a run that pays none of the three is an ordinary run rather than a bad one.
THE DEEP FIND is gated on Woodcutting level alone through a Condition rather than a Ladder,
because there are no tiers here: either the worker is deep enough into the trade to shake
concentrated essence out of a log, or they are not. Below that level the roll never fires at all.
Move the Min to change when the mill starts giving up the good stuff.
THE LUCK LADDER is the one roll here that reads Woodcutting LUCK rather than level, on its own
floors, with no Chance gating it: it always resolves, and its zero floor pays a small handful of
fibre rather than nothing. Concentrated essence rides only the top floor, so a heavily invested
luck tree is what it takes to shake loose an extra one here, on top of whatever the deep find
A Chance is a percentage from zero to one hundred, and rolls evaluate INDEPENDENTLY, so more than
one of these can land on the same claim.
Each carries a Cue, the celebration id a roll may author beside its Grants; it fires only when
the grants beside it genuinely paid out. Rare_Find is the everyday chime the MMO jar ships as a
toast; the concentrated essence names the Sawmill's own deep-find cue so a rare find sounds like
a rare cycle. Author a new Cue value plus a Server/ZiggfreedCommon/FeedbackMoments file of that
name for a celebration of your own.
Name: Mmo_Sawmill_Trim_Finds

Rolls.$Comment: Concentrated essence, for a worker deep enough into the trade to find it.
A personal Woodcutting boost token, roughly one run in twenty.
Luck alone, on its own floors: a small handful of fibre at the bottom, more at the middle floor, and one extra concentrated essence once the reading is this high.
